To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Penetrations of methicilin, oxacillin and cephalothine into cortical bone and into synovial tissue were studied 1 hour after their intravenous administrations in 105 patients undergoing hip arthroplasty.

the three antibiotics studied penetrate well into bone and synovium and that the penetration of methicillin and oxacillin into bone and synoxial tissues is significantly less than that of cephalothin.

the three agents were equally effective against staphylococcus in synovial tissues and the penetration of the drug into bone was not related to the dose of the drug administered or the serum levels achieved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for the study of the penetration of methicillin and oxacillin in bone and synovium.
the penetration of three antibiotics into osseous and synovial tissue.
the penetration of the beta-lactams into the bone and synovia of patients undergoing arthroplasty and the effect of the drug levels on the inhibition of staphylococcus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cephalothin, oxacillin and methicillin are all effective in achieving osseous and synovial tissue levels which are inhibitory to Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococccus epidermidis.
cephalothin penetrates into bone and synovia as well as or better than methicillin or oxacillin.
the three antibiotics were equally effective in achieving osseous and synovial tissue concentrations inhibitory to stafhylococci.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
methicillin, cephalothin, and oxacillin are effective in achieving osseous drug concentrations inhibitory to most staphylococcus species.
methicillin and oxacillin are not as effective as cephalothin in achieving inhibitory levels in bone.
cephalothin, in contrast to the other agents, achieves a high serum level and penetrates bone and synovium to inhibit the growth of staphylococcus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more careful when we are interpreting the results of these types of studies.
the use of a single dose of 500 mg of cephalexin in the treatment of acute bacterial prostatitis is not sufficient.
the three agents penetrate osseous and synovial tissue to similar extents.
